How do you care for a bamboo palm in the UAE?

Bamboo palm care in the UAE needs three things: bright indirect light with no direct sun, a free-draining mix kept slightly moist but never wet, and a spot out of the direct AC flow. Overwatering can rot the roots of Chamaedorea seifrizii. The ASPCA lists the parlour palm, also sold as bamboo palm, as non-toxic to cats and dogs.

Chamaedorea seifrizii (syn. Chamaedorea erumpens) · Also called Reed palm, Bamboo palm (also used for the parlour palm, Chamaedorea elegans), كنبار (Arabic name for the genus Chamaedorea)
By the PlantsWorld team · Updated 12 November 2026

Bamboo Palm quick facts

LightMedium to bright indirect light; tolerates low light. No direct sun through glass.
WaterWhen the top of the mix feels dry. Keep it slightly moist, never soggy.
SoilFree-draining potting mix rich in organic matter, in a pot with a drainage hole.
TemperaturePenn State Extension: 21–27 °C by day, about 16 °C at night. Cold damage at about 7 °C or below.
HumidityMedium. Brown tips can be a sign of dry air, salts or uneven watering.
ACFine in AC rooms; keep it out of the direct flow from a vent.
Outdoors in UAEOnly in full shade with shelter from wind; protect from summer heat and cold inland nights.
PetsParlour palm, also sold as bamboo palm: non-toxic to cats and dogs (ASPCA). The ASPCA has no entry for C. seifrizii.
SizeClumping canes; NC State Extension gives about 0.9–2.3 m tall.
GrowthSlow to moderate; new canes grow from the base.

Is a bamboo palm right for you?

A good fit if

  • You have a cat or a dog: the ASPCA lists the parlour palm, also sold as bamboo palm, as non-toxic to cats and dogs.
  • You have a room with medium light, or a bright spot that gets no direct sun.
  • You want a tall, soft, tropical floor plant for a living room, a bedroom corner or an office.
  • You are happy to check the soil before you water, instead of watering on a fixed day.

Think twice if

  • Your only free spot gets direct sun through west- or south-facing glass.
  • You often forget your plants: a bamboo palm likes slightly moist soil and does not enjoy long bone-dry spells.
  • You want a plant for an open, sunny balcony in summer.

How much light does a bamboo palm need?

A bamboo palm grows best in medium to bright indirect light and tolerates low light. NC State Extension calls it an excellent houseplant for low-light areas, and in its native forests it grows in dappled shade under taller trees.

Direct sun is the bigger risk for a bamboo palm in the UAE. Strong afternoon sun through west- or south-facing glass can scorch the fronds, so place the palm beside a bright window rather than in the sunbeam, or filter the light with a sheer curtain. Tinted tower glazing cuts the light indoors, so a spot close to a tinted window is often just right.

Shop: Bamboo Palm - Chamaedorea Elegans

How often should you water a bamboo palm in Dubai and the UAE?

Water a bamboo palm when the top of the potting mix feels dry, then water thoroughly until water runs out of the drainage hole. Penn State Extension sums it up as "keep moist, but not wet". There is no fixed number of days, because how fast the pot dries depends on your home.

Test before you water a bamboo palm: push a finger into the top of the mix. If it feels dry, water. If it still feels damp, wait and test again later. Lifting the pot also helps: a pot that feels light has dried out, and a heavy pot still holds water.

Several things change how often a bamboo palm needs water. A small pot, a terracotta pot, a bright or warm spot and long summer days dry the mix faster. A large plastic or glazed pot, a dim room, cooler winter months and a humid coastal home keep it moist for longer.

Always empty the saucer after the pot stops dripping. A bamboo palm that stands in water or in soggy mix can get root rot, stem rot and bud rot.

  • UAE tap water is desalinated and then remineralised, and its mineral content varies by area and building. UF/IFAS rates bamboo palm's salt tolerance as poor, so if you see a white crust on the mix or pot, or brown leaf tips, scrape off the crust and flush the pot with plenty of water, then let it drain fully.

What soil and pot does a bamboo palm need?

Plant a bamboo palm in a potting mix that drains well and is rich in organic matter. A good universal potting soil with some perlite mixed in keeps the mix moist but airy; the RHS suggests three parts peat-free ericaceous compost to one part perlite for its close relative, the parlour palm.

Use a pot with a drainage hole for a bamboo palm. A decorative pot without a hole works as an outer cover, as long as you lift the inner pot out to drain after watering. Penn State Extension notes that palms like to be slightly root-bound, so a snug pot is better than a large one.

Shop: Universal Potting Soil – Holland, Perlite – Amorphous Volcanic Glass

What humidity does a bamboo palm need under AC?

A bamboo palm prefers medium humidity. AC rooms in the UAE are not always dry: some homes feel dry, while others, especially on the coast, stay humid. So look at the plant, not the AC.

If a bamboo palm gets brown tips on many fronds while the watering is right and there is no salt crust on the mix, the air is probably too dry for it. Use a humidifier in the room, as Penn State Extension suggests. Keep the palm out of the direct flow of an AC vent and away from draughty doors, because cold draughts damage the fronds.

Dust bamboo palm fronds with a damp cloth. Do not use leaf-shine products, which Penn State Extension says damage palm fronds.

What temperature does a bamboo palm need?

Penn State Extension gives 21–27 °C by day and about 16 °C at night as ideal for indoor palms, which matches most air-conditioned UAE homes and offices. Cold damage shows as reddish-brown dead patches on the fronds and usually happens at about 7 °C or below.

On the UAE coast, winter nights rarely get that cold. Inland, in Al Ain, desert areas and the mountains, and in colder GCC cities such as Riyadh and Kuwait, winter nights can drop below 7 °C, so bring outdoor bamboo palms inside or into a sheltered spot on cold nights.

Should you fertilise a bamboo palm?

Yes, but feed a bamboo palm lightly. Use a balanced fertiliser in the growing season, from spring to early autumn, and stop in winter. Penn State Extension suggests a balanced slow-release liquid fertiliser two to three times over spring and summer, and warns that too much fertiliser harms palms over time.

Follow the label and use less rather than more. Bamboo palm has a poor tolerance of salts, and extra fertiliser adds salts to the mix that can burn the leaf tips.

Shop: Blaukorn NPK Fertiliser 12-12-17

When and how should you repot a bamboo palm?

Repot a bamboo palm only when the roots fill the pot: roots grow out of the drainage hole, or water runs straight through. Palms are sensitive to repotting and like a slightly snug pot, so do not repot just because the plant is new.

When you repot a bamboo palm, go up only a little in pot size. The RHS suggests a pot about 2 cm wider for the parlour palm, and warns that a much bigger pot holds wet mix that can cause root rot. In the UAE, repot in the cooler months, ideally in spring, not in the summer heat.

  1. Choose a pot only slightly wider than the old one, with a drainage hole, and fresh free-draining potting mix.
  2. Ease the palm out of the old pot without breaking up the root ball. Squeeze or tap a plastic pot to loosen it.
  3. Remove any black, soft roots with clean scissors, and leave the healthy roots alone.
  4. Set the root ball in the centre of the new pot, fill around it with fresh mix and press it down gently.
  5. Water thoroughly, let the pot drain, and keep the palm out of direct sun while it settles.

How do you propagate a bamboo palm?

Propagate a bamboo palm by division. A bamboo palm grows as a clump of canes, so a large clump can be split into smaller plants, each with its own canes and roots. Growing from seed is slow, and a bamboo palm only sets seed when a male and a female plant flower together.

Penn State Extension notes that palms are sensitive to repotting and advises care not to damage the roots. For this reason, only divide a large, healthy bamboo palm clump, and do it in the cooler months.

  1. Water the palm and let the pot drain, then take the plant out of its pot.
  2. Gently tease or cut the clump apart with a clean knife, so each piece has several canes and its own roots.
  3. Pot each piece in its own pot of fresh, free-draining mix.
  4. Water thoroughly, let the pots drain, and keep the new plants in bright indirect light while they settle.

Where should you put a bamboo palm at home or in the office?

A bamboo palm suits living-room corners, bedrooms, hotel lobbies and offices with windows, because it tolerates lower light and grows into a tall, soft clump. Put it beside a bright window, not in direct sun, and not in the direct flow of an AC vent.

Outdoors in the UAE, a bamboo palm needs shade and shelter from wind, as UF/IFAS advises for outdoor plants. Summer days in Dubai reach about 41–42 °C and the nights stay warm, so most bamboo palms do better indoors from May to September. If you move a palm outside, do it gradually and keep it in indirect light, as Penn State Extension advises.

Shop: Bamboo Palm - Chamaedorea Elegans - Bushy

Should you cut brown fronds off a bamboo palm?

Yes, cut a fully brown bamboo palm frond off at its base with clean scissors. Older fronds turn brown and die naturally, and UF/IFAS notes that they hang on to the stem and need to be removed by hand.

A few brown lower fronds are normal ageing. Browning across the whole bamboo palm is a sign of a care problem, usually water, humidity or salts; see the problems below.

What should you do in the first week after your bamboo palm arrives?

A new bamboo palm needs time to settle in after the move. The main risk at first is too much care, especially too much water.

  1. Put the palm in bright indirect light, away from direct sun and out of the direct flow of an AC vent.
  2. Leave it in one spot. Moving it again and again slows the settling in.
  3. Test the mix with a finger before you water. Nursery mix is often still moist when the plant arrives.
  4. Do not repot or fertilise yet. Let the palm settle in its delivery pot first.
  5. Cut off any frond that is fully brown, at its base. A few bent or marked fronds after a move are common.

How does bamboo palm care change through the UAE year?

Summer May–Sep

Keep indoor bamboo palms out of direct sun through glass. Pots in bright, warm spots dry faster, so test the mix more often. Outdoor palms need full shade and shelter from hot wind; with daytime highs around 41–42 °C and warm nights, most do better indoors until the heat breaks.

Autumn Oct–Nov

As the heat eases, you can move bamboo palms back to a shaded balcony or terrace, gradually and starting in deep shade. The cooler months are a good time to divide large clumps.

Winter Dec–Feb

Bamboo palm growth slows, the mix dries more slowly and the palm needs water less often, so always test first. Stop feeding. Coastal winters are mild. Inland and in colder GCC cities, nights can fall below 7 °C, so bring outdoor palms in on cold nights, and make sure outdoor pots drain after rain.

Spring Mar–Apr

Spring is the best time to repot a bamboo palm that has filled its pot, and to start feeding again. Move outdoor palms into full shade before May.

Why are my bamboo palm leaf tips turning brown?

Brown tips on bamboo palm fronds usually come from one of three causes: air that is too dry for the plant, salts from tap water or fertiliser building up in the mix, or uneven watering. Bamboo palm has a poor tolerance of salts, so salt build-up is a common cause in the UAE.

How to tell: A white crust on the mix or pot rim (salts); tips browning on many fronds with correct watering (dry air); tips browning after the mix dried out completely or stayed wet (watering).

How to fix it:

  1. Scrape the white crust and a thin layer of mix off the surface.
  2. Flush the pot with plenty of water and let it drain fully.
  3. Feed less, and only in the growing season.
  4. Move the palm out of the direct flow of an AC vent, and raise the humidity if the air is dry.
  5. Trim the brown tips with clean scissors if you wish. Brown tissue does not turn green again.

Why are my bamboo palm leaves turning yellow?

Yellow or brown fronds low on a bamboo palm are usually normal ageing: older fronds die off as new canes grow. Yellowing across the whole plant, with mix that stays wet, points to overwatering and root problems. Too little light can also turn the fronds yellow.

How to tell: Only the oldest, lowest fronds yellow (ageing); many fronds yellow and the mix is still damp long after watering (overwatering); pale, yellowing fronds and weak growth in a dim spot (too little light).

How to fix it:

  1. Cut fully yellow or brown old fronds off at the base.
  2. Test the mix before you water, and let the top dry first.
  3. Empty the saucer after every watering.
  4. If the mix stays wet and the canes feel soft, check the roots as described for root rot.
  5. Move a palm in a dim spot to brighter indirect light, out of direct sun.

Why are my bamboo palm canes going soft or collapsing?

Soft, dark canes, a smell from the pot or a dying centre on a bamboo palm mean rot. Waterlogged, overwatered mix causes root rot, stem rot and bud rot in bamboo palms.

How to tell: Mix still wet long after watering, soft or dark canes at the base, a foul smell, a newest frond that turns pale or wilts and pulls out easily.

How to fix it:

  1. Stop watering.
  2. Take the palm out of its pot and look at the roots.
  3. Cut away black, soft roots and any rotten canes with clean scissors.
  4. Repot in fresh, free-draining mix in a pot with a drainage hole, no bigger than the remaining roots need.
  5. Water only when the top of the mix feels dry.

Helps: Universal Potting Soil – Holland

What are the fine webs and pale speckles on my bamboo palm?

Fine webbing and pale, speckled fronds on a bamboo palm are signs of spider mites. UF/IFAS notes that spider mites and scale can become serious pests of bamboo palms grown indoors.

How to tell: Tiny moving dots and fine webs on the undersides of the fronds, a dull or speckled leaf surface.

How to fix it:

  1. Move the palm away from other plants.
  2. Wipe the fronds, especially the undersides, with a damp cloth, or rinse them with water, as Penn State Extension advises.
  3. A neem-based spray is another option; follow the label.
  4. Check the undersides of the fronds again regularly until no new mites appear.

Helps: Neem Shield – Herbal Pesticide

What are the white cotton patches or brown bumps on my bamboo palm?

White, cottony patches on a bamboo palm are mealybugs, and small brown or grey bumps that scrape off are scale insects. Both suck sap and are common indoor pests of bamboo palms.

How to tell: Cottony clusters where fronds join the canes, brown bumps along the fronds, sticky residue, weak growth.

How to fix it:

  1. Move the palm away from other plants.
  2. Wipe the pests off with a damp cloth or a cotton bud.
  3. Spray the whole plant with a neem-based spray, following the label, and repeat until no new pests appear.

Helps: Neem Shield – Herbal Pesticide

What are the reddish-brown dead patches on my bamboo palm?

Reddish-brown dead areas on bamboo palm fronds are typical of cold damage. Penn State Extension says this usually happens at about 7 °C or below; cold draughts from AC vents, windows and doors also damage fronds.

How to tell: Patches appear after a cold night outdoors or on the side facing an AC vent or a draughty door.

How to fix it:

  1. Move the palm out of the cold or out of the direct flow of the vent.
  2. Bring outdoor palms in on cold inland winter nights.
  3. Cut off badly damaged fronds at the base once new growth starts.

Why does my bamboo palm have pale or scorched patches?

Pale, bleached or brown dry patches on a bamboo palm are usually sun scorch. In the UAE this often happens behind west- or south-facing glass, or outdoors without full shade.

How to tell: Damage on the side facing the window or the sun, appearing soon after the palm was moved.

How to fix it:

  1. Move the palm out of direct sun, or filter the window with a sheer curtain.
  2. Scorched patches do not recover. Cut badly damaged fronds off at the base.

Bamboo Palm myths and facts

MythFact
A bamboo palm is a kind of bamboo.A bamboo palm is a true palm (family Arecaceae). The name comes from its cane-like stems with rings that look like bamboo.
A bamboo palm cleans the air in a room.Potted plants have removed chemicals in small sealed test chambers, but a 2019 review found that a building would need 10 to 1,000 plants per square metre of floor to match normal ventilation.
Brown lower fronds mean the palm is dying.Older lower fronds brown and die naturally. Browning across the whole plant is the warning sign.
A bigger pot makes a bamboo palm grow faster.Palms like a slightly snug pot. A pot much bigger than the roots stays wet and can cause root rot.

Is a bamboo palm safe for cats and dogs?

The ASPCA lists bamboo palm as non-toxic to cats, dogs and horses, but its entry is for Chamaedorea elegans, the parlour palm, which is also sold as bamboo palm. The ASPCA has no separate entry for Chamaedorea seifrizii. NC State Extension gives C. seifrizii a low poison severity for people: the flesh of the fruit can irritate sensitive skin, so wash your hands after handling the fruit. Any plant can upset a pet's stomach if a lot is eaten.

If your pet chewed it: If your pet has eaten a large amount or seems unwell, call your vet or a 24-hour animal emergency clinic and tell them the plant name.

Bamboo Palm FAQs

Is a bamboo palm the same as a parlour palm?

A bamboo palm and a parlour palm are not quite the same. The bamboo palm is Chamaedorea seifrizii, a taller, clumping palm with cane-like stems. The parlour palm, Chamaedorea elegans, is a smaller relative that is also sold as bamboo palm. Their care is almost the same.

Can a bamboo palm live outside in the UAE?

A bamboo palm can live outside in the UAE only in full shade with shelter from wind, and best in the cooler months from October to April. In summer, daytime heat around 41–42 °C and warm nights are hard on a shade palm, so most do better indoors. Inland and in colder GCC cities, bring it in on winter nights below about 7 °C.

Does a bamboo palm clean the air?

A bamboo palm does not noticeably clean the air in a normal room. Studies that found potted plants removing chemicals were done in small sealed chambers, and a 2019 review found that a building would need 10 to 1,000 plants per square metre of floor to match normal ventilation. Choose a bamboo palm for its looks and easy care.

Can a bamboo palm live indoors under AC all year?

Yes, a bamboo palm can live indoors under AC all year. Air-conditioned UAE homes and offices sit close to the 21–27 °C that Penn State Extension gives as ideal for indoor palms. Keep the bamboo palm out of direct sun and out of the direct flow of the AC vent, and test the mix before you water.

Can a bamboo palm grow in low light?

Yes, a bamboo palm tolerates low light, and NC State Extension calls it an excellent houseplant for low-light areas. It grows more slowly in a dim spot, so give it medium or bright indirect light for the fullest growth.

How tall does a bamboo palm grow?

NC State Extension gives a bamboo palm a height of about 0.9–2.3 m, and Penn State Extension says it reaches about 2 m. Outdoors in tropical gardens it can grow taller. New canes keep growing from the base, so the clump also gets wider.

How fast does a bamboo palm grow?

A bamboo palm grows slowly to moderately. New canes grow from the base, so the palm fills out over time more than it shoots up. Low light and winter slow it down.

Does a bamboo palm flower?

A bamboo palm flowers sometimes. It can produce small pale-yellow flowers on stalks that turn orange, followed by small black fruit. Male and female flowers grow on separate plants, so fruit forms only when both are present. The fruit juice can irritate sensitive skin.

Ordering from PlantsWorld

How is plant size measured?

Size is measured from the bottom of the nursery pot to the top tip of the highest leaf. A plant listed as 50-60 CM stands in that range measured this way.

Which pot option should I choose, nursery or decorative?

Choose the nursery pot for the lowest price or if you already have a planter. Choose a decorative pot for a ready-to-display plant that arrives fully potted with soil mix, perlite and a drainage layer. The plant itself is the same.

Do the decorative pots have drainage holes?

Decorative pot orders include a drainage layer at the base, with premium soil mix and perlite. For specific details on a particular pot model, send us the product link and our team will confirm.

Is the plant healthy on arrival? Can I check first?

Plants are guaranteed to arrive healthy. Check your plant with the delivery agent: if it's damaged or not what you ordered, you can refuse it on the spot. If you find damage after unpacking, send photos and your order number on WhatsApp (+971 4 294 1422) or email sales@plantsworld.ae within 24 hours and we'll replace it free. You can also ask for a pre-dispatch photo.

My plant arrived with a few drooping or yellow leaves. Is that normal?

Yes, that's normal. A few drooping, bent or yellow leaves are a common reaction to the journey and a new spot, and plants usually recover within a few days. Keep it in bright indirect light and check the soil before watering. If the plant or pot is actually damaged, send photos within 24 hours.

Will my plant be safe in the UAE heat during delivery?

Yes. Our own delivery team brings your order, not a third-party courier. In extreme summer heat (June to September) we may move deliveries to farther emirates to a cooler day and agree the new day with you. If anything arrives damaged, we replace it free.

Will my plant look exactly like the website photo?

You'll receive the variety and size you ordered, but every plant grows individually, so leaf count, shape and shade can differ from the photo, which is representative. For peace of mind, ask for a pre-dispatch photo at checkout or on WhatsApp.

Something looks wrong with your plant?

Send us photos on WhatsApp and our team will tell you what is happening and what to do. These five photos help us answer fast:

  1. The whole plant, from a step back
  2. A close-up of the problem leaf, front and back
  3. The soil surface and the pot, with the drainage hole if there is one
  4. Where the plant stands: the window, the AC vent and the light
  5. When you last watered, and how much
